discovery: Theoretical discovery of anyons: quantum particles with fractional exchange statistics in two dimensions

nominees.name: Jan Myrheim
nominees.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Trondheim, Norway

nominees.name: Frank Wilczek
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, USA, and Stockholm University, Sweden

subfield: Condensed matter theory / topological quantum matter
motivation: In 1977 Leinaas and Myrheim showed, from a careful analysis of the configuration space of identical particles, that quantum mechanics in two dimensions permits exchange statistics interpolating continuously between bosons and fermions. In 1982 Wilczek independently arrived at the same conclusion through flux-charge composites and named these particles anyons. This overturned the textbook dichotomy of bosons and fermions and became a foundation of topological quantum matter: the quasiparticles of the fractional quantum Hall effect are anyons, non-Abelian generalisations underlie topological quantum computation, and anyonic statistics is central to the concept of topological order. The prediction has now been confirmed directly, through anyon collision experiments (Bartolomei et al., 2020) and Fabry-Perot interferometry (Nakamura et al., 2020) in GaAs quantum Hall systems, and later in other platforms. Few theoretical ideas have so profoundly changed how physicists think about quantum particles.
